questions.question: Who must wear a helmet on a moving motorcycle?

options.text: Only passengers
All riders and passengers
No one

questions.explanation: All riders and passengers must wear a helmet when riding a motorcycle, motor-driven cycle, or motorized bicycle.

questions.question: When riding near a truck:

options.text: If you cannot see the truck's mirrors, the driver cannot see you.
You should not be able to see the truck's mirrors.
You should focus on riding and not worry about the truck's mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: If you cannot see the truck's mirrors, the driver cannot see you.
questions.explanation: Avoid staying in the blind spots of large trucks. If you cannot see the truck's mirrors, the driver cannot see you.

questions.question: Why should you avoid riding directly next to another vehicle?

options.text: The other driver may want to use your lane to pass.
You may be in the vehicle's blind spot.
You may have access to escape routes.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be in the vehicle's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding directly next to another vehicle is dangerous because you may be in its blind spot. The driver will not see you, and the vehicle may block your escape route if a hazard appears.

questions.question: If your front wheel locks while braking, you should:

options.text: Keep the tire locked until you stop.
Continue squeezing the front brake lever.
Release the front brake and immediately re-apply it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake and immediately re-apply it.
questions.explanation: If the front wheel locks up while braking, release the brake pressure. Then immediately re-apply the brake with steady, gradual pressure.

questions.question: The Motorcycle Safety Foundation recommends the SEE strategy for safe riding. What does "SEE" stand for?

options.text: Search, Evaluate, and Execute.
Slow, Experienced, and Error-free.
Safe, Experienced, and Evasive.

questions.explanation: Experienced riders use the SEE strategy to make safe decisions. "SEE" stands for Search, Evaluate, and Execute.

questions.question: If you reach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time as another vehicle:

options.text: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
You should flash your headlight to signal the other vehicle to proceed.
You should go through and expect the other vehicle to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection with no signs or lights, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.

questions.question: A pre-ride inspection should include everything except:

options.text: A tire check.
A test of the turn signals.
A paint inspection.

questions.explanation: Before riding, check your tires, controls, lights, signals, mirrors, brakes, oil, fluids, chassis, and stands. Paint inspection is not necessary.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No right turn
No left turn
No U-turn

questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are white with red and black markings. They tell drivers about traffic laws. This sign means U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: When riding ________, you face the greatest risk of conflict with other vehicles.

options.text: On the expressway
Near an intersection
In a group

questions.explanation: Intersections have the highest risk of conflict between motorcycles and other vehicles. Position yourself in your lane so other drivers can see you clearly.

questions.question: When being passed, moving to the farthest part of your lane from the passing vehicle:

options.text: Is recommended because you are farther from the passing vehicle.
Is not recommended because it signals the other driver to move back into your lane too soon.
Does not affect safety one way or the other.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is not recommended because it signals the other driver to move back into your lane too soon.
questions.explanation: Do not move to the farthest part of your lane when being passed. This may cause the passing driver to move back into your lane too early.

questions.question: How should a motorcycle passenger sit?

options.text: Put their feet on the ground when the motorcycle stops.
Not ride without a back rest.
Sit as far forward as possible without crowding the driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sit as far forward as possible without crowding the driver.
questions.explanation: A passenger should sit as far forward as possible without crowding the driver. Keep both feet on the footrests at all times, even when stopped.

questions.question: When passing parked cars on your right with no oncoming traffic, where should you ride?

options.text: In the left portion of your lane.
In the right portion of your lane.
In the center of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the left portion of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of your lane. This helps you avoid dangers like opening car doors and pedestrians stepping out between vehicles. If there is oncoming traffic, stay in the center to have more space around you.

questions.question: When another rider is passing you, where should you ride?

options.text: In the left portion of the lane.
In the center portion of the lane.
In the right portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the center portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center portion of your lane. Riding to the side nearest the passing driver increases collision risk. Riding on the far side may cause them to return to your lane too soon.

questions.question: What does heavy steering feel like when your front tire is flat?

options.text: Heavy.
Loose.
Soft.

questions.explanation: Heavy steering means your front tire may be flat. Stop riding and check your tires right away.

questions.question: What is the best way to be seen on a motorcycle?

options.text: Use your headlight only at night or in poor visibility.
Always use your headlight.
Add an orange tint to your headlight.

questions.explanation: Riding with your headlight on at all times is the best way to help others see your motorcycle.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Drivers must come to a complete stop.
Drivers may go through the intersection with caution.
Drivers must yield to oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: A solid red arrow means the same as a red light. Drivers must stop and wait for a green signal before turning in that direction.

questions.question: What should you do when someone is tailgating you?

options.text: Allow them to pass.
Speed up.
Not change how you are riding.

questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to let them pass. Speeding up will not help—they may just tailgate you at a higher speed.

questions.question: Where is the gearshift located?

options.text: By the left footrest.
By the right footrest.
By the right handle grip.

questions.explanation: The gearshift lever is located in front of the left footrest. You operate it with your left foot.

questions.question: How can you tell if there are bumps ahead when riding behind another vehicle at night?

options.text: Listen for the other vehicle scraping the pavement.
Watch the other vehicle's taillights bouncing up and down.
Look at the rear bumper to see if it is bouncing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch the other vehicle's taillights bouncing up and down.
questions.explanation: Watch the vehicle ahead of you to see road conditions. If its taillights bounce up and down, there are bumps on the road.

questions.question: Which statement about brakes is true?

options.text: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake.
The rear brake is more powerful than the front brake.
Both brakes are equally powerful.

questions.correctAnswerText: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake.
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides at least 70 percent of a motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: What does a plastic, shatter-resistant face shield do?

options.text: Protects your face, but not your eyes.
Protects your eyes, but not your whole face.
Protects your whole face.

questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face, including your eyes, during a crash. A windshield alone is not enough protection.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Right lane ends
Left lane ends
Traffic control device ahead

questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns that the right lane ends.

questions.question: When entering a turn, when should you change gears?

options.text: Before the turn.
During the turn.
Take the motorcycle out of gear.

questions.explanation: Change gears before you enter a turn. If you must change gears while turning, do it smoothly.

questions.question: What is the best way to help others see your motorcycle?

options.text: Flash your lights.
Keep your high beam headlight on.
Paint your motorcycle a dark color.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your high beam headlight on.
questions.explanation: The best way to help others see your motorcycle is to use your headlight and running lights. Use your high beam headlight day and night whenever it is safe and legal to do so.

questions.question: What clothing should you wear when riding?

options.text: Bright clothing.
Dark clothing.
Uncomfortable clothing.

questions.explanation: Wear bright clothing to make yourself more visible when riding, even during the day. Clothing with reflective material also helps others see you.
